title: #OCD: A Content Analysis of Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder Stereotype Amplification and Misinformation on TikTok
screen_reason: Cross-sectional content analysis of the top 100 English-language TikTok videos tagged #OCD that discuss OCD. Two expert raters (plus a clinical-psychologist tiebreaker) classified each video as useful / personal experience / misleading, where 'misleading' means it conveyed any inaccurate information; 29 of 100 were misleading. That is a share of items in a sample judged inaccurate against expert ground truth, with a stated denominator.

estimates.country: Not stated (English-language TikTok videos under #OCD; authors based in the United States)
estimates.measure_type: % of top #OCD TikTok videos discussing OCD that were rated 'misleading' (conveyed any inaccurate information)
estimates.value_raw: 29 of 100 videos rated "misleading" (18 "useful", 53 "personal experience", 29 "misleading"); abstract: "29 percent were misleading"
estimates.denominator: 100 TikTok videos tagged #OCD that discussed OCD - the first 100 meeting inclusion criteria out of a screened subset of 234 videos returned in TikTok's most-viewed/most-liked ordering (566,000,000 total views)
estimates.definition: A video entered the numerator if raters judged that it conveyed ANY inaccurate information about OCD; a video that presented personal experience but contained misleading statements about OCD was classified as misleading. Inclusion required spoken English content about OCD symptoms, diagnosis, treatment or lived experience; duplicates, non-English audio/text, and videos on other DSM-5 diagnoses were excluded
estimates.source_quote: 18 were rated “useful,” 53 were rated “personal experi- ence,” and 29 were rated “misleading.”
estimates.page_loc: p. 609, Results 'Descriptive statistics - Videos discussing OCD' (the sentence reads 'Of the 100 videos, 18 were rated “useful,” 53 were rated “personal experience,” and 29 were rated “misleading.”'); same figure in the Abstract ('29 percent were misleading') and Table 1 (Misleading n = 29)
estimates.ground_truth_detail: The second and third authors (experienced OCD researchers) independently rated every video against a rating manual (Supplementary Appendix B); disagreements adjudicated by a board-certified clinical psychologist. Initial interrater agreement was 66 percent; after the psychologist reviewed inconsistently rated videos, agreement for the overall process was 100 percent. No kappa reported
estimates.moderator_quote: We ran a query for “#OCD” on August 22, 2023. TikTok displays the most viewed/liked videos ﬁrst.28 Content was sorted accordingly. [...] To compare our results with prior research,24,29–34 the ﬁrst 100 videos meeting inclusion criteria were selected for further rating manually by the ﬁrst author (M.F.).
estimates.notes: breadth coded 'false' rather than 'misleading' because the operational definition of the 'misleading' category is conveying ANY INACCURATE information - i.e. a falsity judgement - even though the category label is 'misleading'. Ranked, top-viewed/liked truncation of a single hashtag -> denom_scope topical + denom_selection curated. Low initial interrater agreement (66%) is the main quality caveat; the reported 100% is post-adjudication and is not an independent reliability estimate. The 18% 'useful' figure is the accurate-content complement, not a second misinformation measure. The paper's other headline construct (stereotype-driven videos) is not a falsity coding - see missed_or_uncertain.

missed_or_uncertain: NOT extracted, with reasons. (1) Stereotype-driven videos: 'Of the 134 videos not meeting inclusion standards (Figure 1), 52 (38.8 percent) did not explicitly discuss OCD but depicted cleaning, straightening, or organizational behavior promoting common OCD stereotypes.' Verbatim share with a denominator, but the numerator is a stereotype-portrayal judgement on videos containing no OCD claims at all - nothing is judged for truth/falsity against a ground truth - and the denominator (videos that FAILED screening) is not an interpretable population. Excluded as not a prevalence-of-misinformation measure; an adjudicator who disagrees would treat it as QUALITY/OTHER, borderline. (2) Account-type subgroups (Table 1, and text): HCP accounts 3/5 (60%) misleading, non-HCP 26/93 (27.96%), nonprofit 0/2 (0%). Source-type subgroups, not the paper's headline denominator, and the HCP cell is n=5. NOTE FOR ADJUDICATION: Table 1's 'Misleading, n (percent)' row prints '5 (60%)' for HCP, which is internally inconsistent - the text twice states 3/5 ('three videos were rated "misleading"'; 'most of the few we found (3/5) posted misinformation'), and 60% of 5 = 3, and the HCP column's other cells (personal 1, useful 1) sum to 5 only if misleading = 3. The printed count 5 is a table error. (3) PEMAT-A/V understandability (74.81%) and actionability (8.00%) are instrument SCALE SCORES reported as means, not shares of items, so no row (per the scale-means rule); they would be QUALITY if a threshold share existed. (4) 6.1 billion #OCD views and the 566,000,000 / 906,600,000 group view totals are volume figures with no falsity numerator. (5) Engagement comparisons (negative binomial regression, Tables 3-6) are association tests, not prevalence. (6) Country left Global: no search locale is stated; only English-language videos were kept, and the authors list that as a limitation.

rob.design: Cross-sectional social-media content analysis, no human participants. One query for #OCD run on 22 August 2023, relying on TikTok's default most-viewed/most-liked ordering; 234 videos screened, first 100 meeting inclusion criteria rated (English spoken content about OCD symptoms/diagnosis/treatment/lived experience; excluded non-English or missing audio/text, other DSM-5 diagnoses, duplicates, and videos not discussing OCD). Two experienced OCD researchers rated independently into useful / personal experience / misleading using a written rating manual; a board-certified clinical psychologist adjudicated inconsistent ratings. Initial interrater agreement 66 percent, 100 percent after adjudication; no kappa reported. PEMAT-A/V applied to the same 100 videos; engagement metadata recorded manually and compared with negative binomial regression. Stated limitations: single hashtag, single time point, top-ranked English videos only, no control for follower count or posting time, account type judged by the first author without a standardized method.
rob.item6_quote: Videos were rated “useful” if they conveyed accurate information about OCD, “personal experience” if they predominantly relied on anecdotal experiences to describe OCD, or “misleading” if they conveyed any inaccurate information.
rob.item10_quote: We applied our inclusion/exclusion criteria to a subset of 234 videos, producing a sample of 100 videos for further analysis, with a total of 566,000,000 views. Of the 100 videos, 18 were rated “useful,” 53 were rated “personal experience,” and 29 were rated “misleading.”
